_note: The parameter catalogue for this corpus: every number a statute did not state, with its unit (the corpus's own units are accepted and scaled by the decoder), the convention its value comes from and its source. It starts empty: the plan decides which parameters exist and proposes each with a provisional value, and the harness enters the proposal here marked `proposed` (run, iteration, node) until the operator reviews it by removing the marker or changing the value; the doctor lists every unreviewed proposal. The operator-authored list this file carried before any law was planned is kept, out of the pipeline's path, under readings/legacy/. Figures the law states are literals on the rule's span, never entries here.

params.name: p.stop_speed_tolerance
params.convention: Stop-detection convention: the greatest speed at which a sampled track is treated as not moving, set at the noise floor of a tracked speed estimate, so that a complete cessation is observable on sampled data rather than requiring an exact zero.
params.source: Vehicle-trajectory practice in stop-sign compliance field studies (FHWA/NCHRP intersection-safety studies)

params.name: p.stop_hold_time
params.convention: Stop-detection convention, dwell half: the least time the speed must remain at or below the tolerance for the cessation to be complete rather than one slow sample, taken as several sampling intervals of a trajectory source.
params.source: Vehicle-trajectory practice in stop-sign compliance field studies

params.name: p.stop_place_tolerance
params.convention: Stopping-place convention: the greatest distance from the required stopping place at which a halt still counts as being at it, taken from the painted width and placement tolerance of a stop bar together with the positioning error of a tracked body outline.
params.source: MUTCD stop-line marking dimensions with trajectory positioning error

params.name: p.view_sight_distance_min
params.convention: Intersection sight-distance model: the least distance along the through highway that must be visible from the stopping place for the departure sight triangle to be satisfied at the through highway's design speed.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book, intersection sight distance (Case B, stop control on the minor road)

params.name: p.approach_lookback_distance
params.convention: Approach look-back convention: the greatest distance from the intersection region at which a halt is still counted as the halt this entrance requires, taken as the functional approach length of an intersection at urban approach speeds - the upstream distance over which a driver's stopping manoeuvre belongs to that intersection. It bounds the rule's look-back at the third place, where the law names no distance, so the duty is decidable on a finite trace; it is not a stopping place the law names and does not stand in for the view.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book, functional area of an intersection (upstream approach length)

params.name: p.simultaneous_entry_tolerance
params.convention: Gap-acceptance convention: the greatest difference between the instants at which the two vehicles' footprints first overlap the intersection region at which the two entries still count as being at approximately the same time; set at the order of the critical gap a driver accepts before crossing in front of a conflicting vehicle at an uncontrolled junction.
params.source: Critical-gap and gap-acceptance studies for crossing manoeuvres at unsignalized intersections (Highway Capacity Manual two-way-stop procedures; NCHRP gap-acceptance field studies).

params.name: p.turn_window
params.convention: Manoeuvre-detection convention, window half: the window behind the observation over which the signed heading change of a turn is integrated, set at the order of the time a passenger car takes to swing through a junction turn at intersection turning speed.
params.source: Turning paths of the passenger-car design vehicle at intersection turning speeds (AASHTO Green Book turning-path templates).

params.name: p.turn_heading_change_min
params.convention: Manoeuvre-detection convention, angle half: the least leftward signed heading change within the window at which a road user counts as making a left turn; set above the heading change of a lane change or of following the road's curvature and below the change of a junction turn, so that the two are separated.
params.source: Design-vehicle turning paths against measured lane-change heading excursions (AASHTO Green Book; lane-change kinematics studies).

params.name: p.turn_signal_lookback
params.convention: Signalling convention: the window behind the observation within which a lit left turn indicator still counts as a declared intention to turn left; set at the order of the interval a driver is expected to signal before beginning a turn, so that a signal given on the approach is not stale by the time the vehicles meet.
params.source: Signalling intervals required before a turn in state vehicle codes and the driver handbooks aligned with them.

params.name: p.yield_clearance
params.convention: Gap-acceptance convention: the least surface gap a yielding road user leaves to the user it grants precedence to, taken as the clearance between body outlines a driver leaves when waiting for or passing behind another vehicle at a junction.
params.source: Clearance practice for intersection manoeuvres (AASHTO Green Book; gap-acceptance field studies).

params.name: p.yield_window
params.convention: Gap-acceptance convention, window half: the window behind the observation over which the clearance must hold, so that a momentary gap in an otherwise closing approach does not count as granting precedence.
params.source: Clearance practice for intersection manoeuvres (AASHTO Green Book; gap-acceptance field studies).

params.name: p.yield_closure_allowance
params.convention: Gap-acceptance convention, noise half: the fall in the longitudinal component of the surface gap that is attributed to measurement noise rather than to the yielding road user closing on the other.
params.source: Tracking error of ground-plane body outlines in road-scene perception datasets.

_fields.aggregates: optional operator overrides only: word, classes (ru.* ids or other words). The run derives every aggregate the laws use from the corpus definitions (results/<run>/reading.json, for review); an operator entry here takes precedence over the derived one.
